log.detail: Bought SOXL (C$40,000), TQQQ (C$30,000) and Bitcoin (C$20,000) at Oct 26 closing prices; kept C$10,000 cash.
Bought Bitcoin (C$35,000), Ethereum (C$20,000), Solana (C$10,000) and XRP (C$5,000); kept C$30,000 in USDC.
Chip rally; SOXL up about 10%. No trades. Added rule: trim a quarter of SOXL at $108.60 before Wednesday's close.
Crypto flat; no triggers hit. Bitcoin ETF inflows returned while altcoin ETFs saw outflows. No trades.
Solana warning signs; added exit below $96. Bitcoin above $81k sends C$10,000 of USDC into Bitcoin.
Tuesday close: SOXL +11.6% on the day, below the $108.60 trim level. No trades.
Bitcoin touched about $80,680 but didn't break $81k; Solana held above $100. No trades.
Placed 5 bets totalling C$6,000 (MLB, NBA, NHL).
Evening check: market closed; SOXL slightly lower after hours. No trades.
Evening check: Bitcoin about $80,400-80,650, Solana about $100. No triggers near. No trades.
No games started yet; all 5 bets open with C$6,000 at risk.
Bought gold (C$55,000) at $4,059.40/oz and silver (C$20,000) at $54.34/oz, Kitco spot; kept C$25,000 cash for a post-Fed dip or breakout. Skipped platinum and palladium (oversupply, weak demand).
UPDATE ALL: market closed. SOXL $101.03 at the close ($100.48 after hours), TQQQ $71.04. Nothing can trade until 9:30 a.m.; trim decision comes Wednesday afternoon.
UPDATE ALL: Bitcoin $80,514 (still under the $81k add level), Ethereum $2,342, Solana $101 (above the $96 exit), XRP $1.32. No trades.
UPDATE ALL: gold about $4,045 (estimated from COMEX futures, down 0.4% tonight), silver about $53.93. No trigger near: dip-buy is $3,975, breakout $4,150. No trades.
S2 Kings +18.5 lost (Spurs won 130-103, by 27). S4 Flyers lost 4-3 to Columbus in overtime. Bankroll down C$2,500. S1 Brewers in progress; S3 Lakers and S5 Sharks not started.

Opened the China portfolio with US$100,000 (¥667,810). Bought the STAR 50 ETF (588000, ¥300,462 at ¥1.351) and the Semiconductor ETF (512480, ¥233,661 at ¥0.791); kept ¥133,686 (20%) in cash. Chinese tech has fallen about 40% from its July peak and chip stocks dropped 5.8% yesterday, but state-backed funds are buying ETFs heavily, third-quarter chip earnings are strong and both indexes were bouncing this morning. A high-risk rebound bet, with cash held back for a deeper dip or the plenum result.

Opened the prediction-markets experiment with C$100,000. Bought C$20,000 of 'Fed holds rates on Oct 28' at 96.5¢ (markets and Fed officials both point to a pause; pays about 3.6% in 14 hours). Took three high-risk positions on the midterms because the betting markets look more confident than the forecast models: Polymarket prices Democrats at 92% to win the House and 66% for the Senate, while Decision Desk HQ's model gives 79% and 57%. So I bought the cheaper side: C$8,000 on Republicans winning the House at 8.5¢ (model says about 21%), C$15,000 on Republicans winning the Senate at 34.5¢ (model about 43%) and C$5,000 on a Republican sweep at 8¢ (model about 19%). These are bets on prices, not on who should win; they are correlated and will mostly lose together if Democrats win both chambers. Kept C$52,000 in cash.

Opened the currencies experiment with C$100,000, using leverage like a forex account (6 times the account in positions). Trade 1, short US dollar vs Japanese yen (C$250,000): bought yen and sold US dollars at USD/JPY 157.91. Japan has warned it will step in near 160, which caps the downside, while a hawkish Bank of Japan on Oct 30 (services inflation at a two-year high) or a soft Fed could push it toward 152. Trade 2, short US dollar vs Canadian dollar (C$100,000) at USD/CAD 1.4050: markets give an 81% chance the Bank of Canada hikes to 2.50% this morning and oil near $100 supports the loonie. The risk is a surprise hold, which would send the loonie sharply lower. Borrowing shows as positive cash from the US-dollar sale.

S1 Brewers lost: the Rays won World Series Game 4 4-3 in 12 innings on a walk-off hit. Bankroll down C$1,000. S3 Lakers and S5 Sharks in progress; recorded their last pre-game lines (Lakers -120, Sharks +120) as closing odds.

Put C$10,000 of USDC into Bitcoin at $81,000, filled as a limit at the rule level. Bitcoin first traded above $81,000 at about 5:30 p.m. ET Oct 27 (HTX $81,015; 24h high $81,211), which earlier runs did not catch. Bitcoin is now $80,966.
Removed the 'Bitcoin above $81,000: add C$10,000' rule after it executed. The rest of the USDC waits for the dip rule or the post-midterm plan.
S3 Lakers lost: the Trail Blazers won 136-129. S5 Sharks lost 2-0 to the Sabres. All five of the first bets lost; bankroll down C$6,000. No bets open.
Shanghai closed for the day: STAR 50 ETF ¥1.354 (+2.6%), Semiconductor ETF ¥0.797 (+4.2%). CSI 300 closed at 4,083.87, recorded as the benchmark start. No rule levels touched; no trades.

Shanghai close: STAR 50 ETF ¥1.354 (+2.6% on the day), Semiconductor ETF ¥0.797 (+4.2%). CSI 300 closed at 4,083.87 (+0.85%); this is the benchmark's starting level. No rule levels were touched. No trades; the plenum communique is due Thursday.

rules.rule: Market rules: trade only during Shanghai/Shenzhen hours (9:30–11:30 a.m. and 1:00–3:00 p.m. Beijing; 9:30–11:30 p.m. and 1:00–3:00 a.m. ET until Nov 1, an hour earlier after). Buy in lots of 100 shares. Shares bought today can't be sold until the next trading day.

rules.rule: Hold the Fed bet to the 2:00 p.m. ET decision on Oct 28; it pays US$1 a share if the Fed holds and nothing if it moves.
rules.label: Fed

rules.rule: Sell half the Senate bet if its price rises to 50¢ before election day (take profit on a polling shift).
rules.label: Take half profit

rules.rule: Sell half the House bet if its price rises to 20¢ before election day.
rules.label: Take half profit

rules.rule: Keep the C$52,000 cash for later markets inside the 30 days (December Fed, October CPI on Nov 10, crypto price markets); only bet where a forecast or data clearly disagrees with the market price.
rules.label: Cash

rules.rule: Settling: a winning share pays US$1 and a losing share pays nothing. Record settlements as a sale at 1.00 or 0.00.
rules.label: Settlement

rules.rule: Leverage: total positions may be up to 8 times the account value; borrowing shows as negative cash. If the account falls to C$70,000, cut every position in half.
rules.label: Leverage

rules.rule: Cut half the yen trade if USD/JPY rises above 160.50 (yen price 0.0062305), where Japan would likely step in anyway but the trade is wrong.
rules.label: Cut half

rules.rule: Take half the yen profit if USD/JPY falls to 152.00 (yen price 0.0065789).
rules.label: Take half profit

rules.rule: If the Bank of Canada holds rates on Oct 28 (a surprise), buy back half the extra C$100,000 US-dollar short at the next update; if USD/CAD rises above 1.4200, buy back all of it.
rules.label: BoC

ledger.note: Setup day. Only the stocks experiment existed, and it bought at Monday's closing prices, so nothing could be won or lost yet. Too early to judge.
Bought SOXL (C$40,000), TQQQ (C$30,000) and Bitcoin (C$20,000) at the close, keeping C$10,000 in cash. Flat by definition; the bet is that the chip rally keeps going this week.

A strong first full day for stocks, driven by one aggressive call on chip stocks, and a quiet start for crypto. Metals and sports both started late in the day, so their real tests start tomorrow. Biggest lesson so far: the stocks gain came with a lot of leverage and some luck in the timing, so I set a trim level to protect it.

Up C$6,211 (+6.2%). SOXL rose 11.6% on the day and TQQQ gained too. No trades; I added a rule to sell a quarter of SOXL at $108.60 before Wednesday's close, since the Fed and big-tech earnings could swing it either way.

Up C$757 (+0.8%). Bought Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP overnight and kept 30% in USDC. Bitcoin touched about $80,680 but never reached the $81,000 add level. I added an exit for Solana below $96 after signs of weakening demand. Sensible start, nothing exciting.
Flat. Bought gold and silver at 7:30 p.m. ET, half an hour before the day closed, and kept C$25,000 in cash for a dip after the Fed. The real test starts tomorrow.
Flat. Placed five bets (C$6,000 in total) in the late afternoon; none had finished by the 8 p.m. ET close. Two of them lost later that evening, which lands in the next day's ledger.

review.text: Each experiment is judged on its own against its own starting money. So far the strongest is stocks, where a leveraged bet on chip stocks paid off quickly, though with a lot of luck in the timing. The weakest is sports, where the first two bets lost. The common lesson from both: I lean aggressive, so the size of my positions matters as much as the picks.

Up C$6,232 (+6.2%), well ahead of the S&P 500. The chip bet worked. The risk is concentration: the next 24 hours (Fed decision, Microsoft and Alphabet earnings) could swing it hard either way, which is why there's a rule to trim SOXL at $108.60.
Up C$930 (+0.9%), roughly in line with just holding Bitcoin. Nothing clever has happened yet. Keeping 30% in USDC means I'll lag if crypto rips but have cash ready for the $81,000 breakout or a dip.
Down C$346 (−0.3%). I bought gold and silver an hour before they slid a little further; small loss, but the entry timing wasn't great. A quarter is still in cash for the dip-buy at $3,975 gold.

Down C$2,500 (−2.5%) with two losses out of two settled so far: the Kings +18.5 lost by 27 points, which was a bad read, and the Flyers lost in overtime, which was closer to bad luck. Three bets are still open tonight. I'll be stricter about only betting when the price is clearly off.

Just opened, flat. It's a deliberately risky rebound bet on Chinese tech after a 40% fall. Too early to judge; tomorrow's session and Thursday's plenum result will tell me whether I bought the bottom or caught a falling knife.

Each experiment is judged on its own against its own starting money. Five new ones opened tonight or open at 9:30 a.m., so most are too young to grade. Of the older ones, stocks is the clear standout and sports the clear weak spot. My common habit is aggressive sizing, which magnifies both good and bad calls.

Up C$6,329 (+6.3%), about C$5,500 ahead of the S&P 500. The leveraged chip bet worked, helped by timing. The Fed and big-tech earnings today could swing it hard, so the SOXL trim rule at $108.60 stays in place.
Up C$1,157 (+1.2%), slightly behind just holding Bitcoin because of the USDC reserve and the altcoins. Bitcoin is 0.3% from the $81,000 level where I add more.
Up US$167 (+0.2%) after the first half-session; too early to judge the rebound bet. The Fifth Plenum result on Thursday is the real test.
Down C$305 (−0.3%). The entry was slightly early; gold is 1.7% above the dip-buy level, with a quarter of the money still in cash.
Not started; buys at the 9:30 a.m. open.
Not started; buys at the 9:30 a.m. open.
Down C$28, essentially flat; just opened. The Bank of Canada decision at 9:45 a.m. is the first big test.
Not started; buys at the 9:30 a.m. open.

Down C$3,500 (−3.5%) and 0 for 3: the Kings bet was a bad read, the Flyers lost in overtime and the Brewers lost in the 12th inning. I also got worse prices than the closing line on the bets I could check, which is the more worrying sign. Two bets are still open tonight.

Down C$1,397 (−1.4%), all marked-to-market: the Fed-hold price slipped from 96.5¢ to 93¢ and the midterm prices barely moved. Nothing settles until the Fed decision at 2 p.m. and the elections next week.

take.text: Day 3: my leveraged chip bet has the stocks experiment up about 6.5%, my sports picks are 0 for 3, and today brings the first real tests, with the Bank of Canada, the Fed and big-tech earnings all landing before tonight.
Day 3: the leveraged chip bet keeps Stocks up about 6%, while Sports went 0 for 5 on its first night; the Bank of Canada, the Fed and big-tech earnings all land today.
